solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unoriginal statement from Conservative in Chile after internal setback?

indicators.note: the party abbreviation goes inside the reworked country name
a setback inside the word: its inner letters are turned back to front while the ends stay put

parts.note: the country's name taken as written

explanation.surface: A Tory politician visiting Chile trots out a tired line after some trouble within the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after internal setback' turns the inner HIL of CHILE round to LIH, giving CLIHE; 'in' then puts C inside, after CLI.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliché is a hackneyed phrase, a remark so overused it lacks any originality.

clue.text: Examine threat to king abroad

parts.note: in chess, check is an attack on the king
out means away from home, abroad

explanation.surface: Investigate a menace to a monarch overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To check out something is to inspect or investigate it.

clue.text: Front part of Jumbo jet? Just the opposite

definitions.text: Front part of Jumbo jet? Just the opposite

parts.words: Front part of Jumbo jet? Just the opposite
parts.note: Jumbo the elephant's front part is its tusks; jet is black and the tusk material is the opposite colour, white

explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo was a famous elephant, not a Boeing 747; jet is the black gem, and tusk material is its white opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivory is the white substance of elephant tusks, which project from the front of the animal.

clue.text: Nurse in hospital with shady alcove

parts.note: H is the map symbol for hospital
an arbour is a shady garden bower

explanation.surface: A nurse working in a hospital that has a shaded nook.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour a feeling, like a grudge, is to nurse it, keeping it alive in one's mind.

clue.text: These mysteries, in particular, can amaze

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Some mysteries, one in particular, are capable of astonishing people.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are secrets or mysteries known only to initiates; the word is a plural, matching 'These mysteries'.

clue.text: For dashing fellow, entering service is hard

indicators.note: the fellow goes into the service's letters

parts.note: the RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: For a dashing young man, joining the armed forces is tough.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means rakish and flamboyant in a slightly disreputable way, much like dashing.

clue.text: Support editor cutting colleague, it's said

indicators.note: the support and editor slice into the colleague's letters

parts.note: an ally is a partner or colleague
a leg is a support, as of a table

explanation.surface: Rumour has it a supporting editor cut off a co-worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegedly means reportedly or supposedly, describing a claim made without proof.

clue.text: A free broadcasting system, so-called

parts.note: to untie is to set free

explanation.surface: A free-to-air broadcaster, or so people call it.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is the British nickname for the BBC, the UK's public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The BBC is affectionately nicknamed Auntie, or Auntie Beeb, so it is the broadcaster's informal name.

clue.text: Protest about renegade party member

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a rat is someone who deserts or betrays their side

explanation.surface: A demonstration targets a turncoat politician who switched parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to the US Democratic Party, so is a member of a political party.

clue.text: Great excitement in the Oval — monarch is one of those watching play

indicators.note: the stirred letters sit inside the words for the and Oval

parts.note: taken as written
an oval shape is the letter O

indicators.note: excitement stirs things up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Huge excitement at the Oval as the monarch joins the crowd watching the cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, so 'play' suggests cricket; ATREG (GREAT stirred) sits inside THE O, then ER, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatregoer attends theatre performances, so is in the audience for a play.

clue.text: Part of steel cable needed for lion, say

parts.note: FE is the chemical symbol for iron, the main element in steel
a line is a rope or cable

explanation.surface: A length of steel wire rope is required to restrain a lion.
explanation.definitionFit: A lion is one example of a cat, and a feline is any member of the cat family.

clue.text: Acceptable way to address a knight?

parts.note: O is the old vocative form, as in 'O king'
Sir Kay is a knight of King Arthur's Round Table

explanation.surface: A question of etiquette: what is the proper form of words for greeting a knight?
explanation.walkthrough: 'O Kay!' is how one might hail Sir Kay of Arthurian legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay is an informal word meaning satisfactory or all right, so acceptable.

clue.text: Opportunity to order one diamond, for example

parts.note: an opening is a chance or opportunity
to bid someone do something is to order them

explanation.surface: A chance to order a single diamond from a jeweller.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, 'one diamond' is a typical first call in the auction, not a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, the first call of an auction is the opening bid, and one diamond is a common example.

clue.text: Poor tutors and the like he had extended

indicators.note: poor work is badly done, so the letters of the next word are put in a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
etc, short for et cetera, means and the like
he'd, the contraction of he had, without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Bad teachers and their sort had their arms held out wide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' turns TUTORS into OUTSTR; then ETC, then HE'D written without the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something outstretched is stretched out to full length, that is extended.

clue.text: Damage covered by a saint, sort of, who helped injured traveller?

indicators.note: the damage is enclosed within the other letters
a sort of saint, a rearranged one, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written
to mar is to damage

explanation.surface: A near-saint who bore a wound helped someone hurt on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' turns A SAINT into SAITAN, and MAR goes inside after SA.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jesus's parable, the Good Samaritan stopped to aid a man beaten by robbers on the road.

clue.text: Porcelain that's liable to be broken during breakfast

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a very thin, delicate kind of china

definitions.text: that's liable to be broken during breakfast
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the casing cracked open to eat a boiled egg

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests dropped crockery at the table, but the second half means the casing of a boiled egg.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a thin translucent china and the brittle casing of an egg cracked at breakfast.

clue.text: Help ambassador mature after mishandling, initially, first overseas trip

indicators.note: the remaining pieces come after that first letter
only the opening letter of mishandling is taken

parts.note: the word supplying its first letter
aid means help
an envoy is a diplomatic representative such as an ambassador
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: An ambassador gets help to grow up after bungling his first foreign posting.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage is a ship's first journey, typically an inaugural trip across the sea.

clue.text: Encourages understandings in speech

indicators.note: spoken, the word for understandings matches the answer

parts.note: insights are understandings

explanation.surface: A speaker motivates people by sharing what they have learned.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to urge or stir someone on to act, so incites means spurs or encourages.

clue.text: Person making call to protect it with face-saving device

indicators.note: the face guard wraps round the other word, shielding it

parts.note: a visor shields the face
taken as written

explanation.surface: A caller arrives with a mask to shield something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face-saving' suggests avoiding embarrassment, but here it is literal: a guard over the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor pays someone a call, going to see them at their home.

clue.text: Every year locks up undesirable

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for every year

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the locks are read from bottom to top

parts.note: locks are hair

explanation.surface: Each year someone undesirable gets locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is an outcast, a person shunned as unwanted by society; undesirable here is a noun.

clue.text: Liable to change key undertakings to settle on island

indicators.note: the key and undertakings sit after the island, following it in the answer

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
C is a musical key
IOUs are written promises to pay, so undertakings

explanation.surface: A volatile person with a key to some promises means to move to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capricious describes someone fickle, whose mood or mind can shift suddenly and unpredictably.

clue.text: Players found pitch

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the actors in a play
second meaning: to found metal is to shape it in a mould

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses of one short word stand side by side; 'found' looks like the past tense of find but is the verb meaning to mould metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a play's company of actors, to mould molten metal, and to throw.

clue.text: The same as throttle? That depends

definitions.text: The same as throttle? That depends

parts.words: The same as throttle? That depends
parts.note: the word means strangle, the same as throttle, but in a car engine it names a different valve from the throttle

explanation.walkthrough: As verbs both mean strangle; as car parts they are separate controls, one for the air supply and one for the engine's speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Choke means strangle, as throttle does, but in an engine the choke restricts air to aid cold starting.

clue.text: Tyrant's pronouncement requiring child's return? Rubbish

indicators.note: the child's word comes back, read from its end to its start

parts.note: a kid is a child
tat is cheap, worthless stuff

explanation.surface: A despot's edict demands a child be sent back, which people dismiss as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is a harsh decree imposed by a ruler without consent, the kind of order a tyrant issues.

clue.text: Nothing gained in trade in poorly regulated shares

indicators.note: the zero is taken into the middle of the other letters
doing something poorly means doing it badly, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A stock market report: no gains in trading shares under weak regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' turns TRADEIN into RATIEND, and 'gained in' puts O inside it after RATI.
explanation.definitionFit: To ration is to control how much of something each person gets, so rationed means allotted portions under rules.

clue.text: Reformed the son, following optimal policy?

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A son who mended his ways and now does what's best.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the proverb 'honesty is the best policy'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says honesty is the best policy, so a truthful person follows that ideal course.

clue.text: Unpleasant experience, getting low grades in exam

indicators.note: the grades go inside the exam word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
D and E are low marks on an exam scale

explanation.surface: A grim time for a student who gets poor marks in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or trying experience, a hard trial to endure.
